title: Mariner performance dashboard: per-model & per-route canvas + chart specs
creator: Ava Chen
description: Design a unified per-model / per-route performance canvas (codename: Mariner) focused on latency, throughput and token metrics with cost overlays and rollout context. The canvas should serve SREs, platform engineers and product teams who need quick triage views plus the ability to deep-dive into micro-traces and model-variant comparisons.
design_goals: 1) Surface high-signal metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens-per-request, throughput RPS) with minimal visual noise. 2) Provide fast comparisons between model variants and routes. 3) Enable cost-aware decisions via token-cost overlays and per-route attribution. 4) Integrate rollout metadata (canary, traffic-split) and fallback events into the same canvas.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Default canvas shows p50/p95/p99 latency sparklines, throughput heatband, token flow and cost-over-time for selected model+route. 2) Hover and click interactions reveal sample traces and recent rollout events. 3) Comparison mode supports up to 3 model-variants side-by-side with synchronized time windows. 4) Charts follow performance color palette and respect accessibility contrast. 5) Componentized chart specs are implemented as design tokens in Figma and a single source of truth JSON for the frontend team.
chart_specs:
Overview of charts included in Mariner: 
- Latency ribbon: stacked quantile ribbons (p50/p75/p95/p99) with area-fill and outline, y-axis in ms (log scale optional), tooltip shows exact quantiles and sample trace link. Aggregation window: 1m default, configurable to 5m/1h. 
- Throughput heatband: 1m bins colored by RPS intensity with spike markers for sudden surges. Click a bin to drill into request samples. 
- Token flow Sankey-lite: sources=prompt/system/assistant, sinks=token-consumed/cached/served, hover reveals token counts and cache-hit ratio. 
- Cost overlay: translucent line on top of latency chart showing cost-per-minute and estimated cost-per-1000-requests. 
- Microtrace mini-timeline: top 3 error traces and slowest traces, grouped by request signature, link to full trace in tracing UI. 
- Comparison strip: small multiples for p95 across variants with percent delta badges and significance marker.
Interaction patterns: linked time-range brush, synchronized crosshairs, contextual menu to pin chart or copy permalink.
visual_guidelines: Color tokens: latency palette (green -> amber -> red), throughput bluescale, cost accent = magenta. Typography: Sizing based on console tokens: title H5, metric H3 numeric, microlabels body-2. Use 3 levels of emphasis for metric numbers. Icons: rollout marker (anchor icon), fallback (broken-bridge icon), cache-hit (bolt icon).
prototype_notes: Prototype adds two experimental features: an anomaly lane for auto-flagged metric regressions (configurable sensitivity), and an embedded rollout timeline showing which model version was serving at each time slice. Prototype demonstrates expanding the Sankey into a stacked bar when the time-window is less than 10 minutes.
tradeoffs_and_decisions:
- Chose multi-quantile ribbon over multiple separate charts to reduce vertical real estate and speed comparison.
- Opted to show cost as overlay instead of separate chart to keep correlation immediate, but provide toggle to move cost into its own pane if users want longer-term trends.
- Sankey-lite simplifies full Sankey so frontend perf stays acceptable on large time windows; expand to full Sankey only in 10m window.
engineering_constraints: Frontend must reuse existing charting primitives (Radial or internal chart lib), maintain 60fps interactions for brush/hover. Backend needs endpoints: /metrics/series (quantiles), /metrics/throughput, /tokens/flow, /cost/estimate and /rollouts/events. Pagination and sampling strategies required for microtraces. Cache header semantics must be passed through for token cache breakdowns.
